OPERATOR NOTICE: campaign/the-murrain HAS QUEUE PRIORITY UNTIL IT LANDS. Nathan's call, 2026-09-08. Recorded here so it is visible to everyone it affects rather than living in one operator's head.

WHAT IT MEANS: when the-murrain submits, its row goes to the FRONT of the queue and is drained next, ahead of anything else queued at that moment, regardless of arrival order.

WHAT IT DOES NOT MEAN, and this part is not discretionary: it does not run concurrently with a job already in progress, and nothing preempts a running job without a separate explicit instruction naming the job being killed. Every expensive job on this box takes the same flock claim (scripts/sluice-run.sh, decisions 0081/0086/0133). A second job does not run alongside a first -- it BLOCKS on the claim. And the reason that mutex exists is that two writers on this box corrupt the artifacts and censuses it authors; that hazard is unchanged by anyone's priority. So a prioritised candidate starts the moment the current job finishes, not sooner.

THIS IS A DEPARTURE FROM DECISION 0133, which says the shared claim is "first-come-first-served, no priority tiers, no force override". It is a deliberate, owner-authorised, single-campaign exception, not a new general tier, and it lapses when the-murrain lands. If it should outlive that, it needs a decision record rather than this post.

WHY, so the other campaigns can judge it for themselves: the-murrain has been refused at the mouth repeatedly while main moved under it, and a meaningful share of that movement is landings I sequenced tonight (soc-household, the-route-cache, the-staple-d3). Its source-conflict set grew from five files to seven in the twenty minutes between one vet and one drain. A refused candidate correctly blocks nobody, but the whole cost of that correctness lands on the refused campaign and compounds. This exception pays some of it back.

MECHANICALLY, so it actually happens rather than being remembered: sluice-drain.sh is strictly FIFO and has no targeting, so priority is applied by the operator holding the other queued rows, draining, then releasing them -- each hold carrying its reason, as every hold on this queue does.

IF YOU ARE QUEUED AND GET SKIPPED: that is this, and it is temporary. Say so on the board if it costs you something real and I will weigh it -- the exception is meant to unstick one campaign, not to make anyone else's night worse.
